title: Press Release Structure + BERT for Earnings Announcement Returns
summary: 138,000+ earnings press releases (2005–2023) used to predict stock returns on earnings announcement days. Compares bag-of-words vs BERT-based embeddings. Key finding: structural features of press releases (section organization, forward-looking language position, guidance placement) add predictive power beyond pure sentiment. BERT outperforms BoW but gains diminish when document structure is ignored.
why_relevant: H163 confirmed FinBERT sentiment on 8-K filings. H174 runs a live PEAD scoring pipeline. H176 (queued) is explicitly 'LLM-enhanced PEAD'. This paper shows that WHERE information appears in the press release (structure) matters, not just sentiment polarity. Our current pipeline scores the full 8-K as a single document — adding section-level FinBERT scoring is a concrete extension.
